title: Approximation transfers through the adapter
statement: Let $L$ and $S$ be encoded maximization problems and let $$ be a rational number. Suppose an adapter reduces instances of $L$ to instances of $S$, recovers an $L$-feasible solution from every feasible solution to the reduced instance, transfers the condition ${1}- {} L(x)$ to ${1}- {} S(R(x))$, and transfers value at least ${7}/{8}+$ on a reduced solution to value at least ${1}/{2}+$ on its recovered solution. If a polynomial-time algorithm for $S$ always outputs a feasible solution and, whenever the optimum is at least $1-$, achieves value at least $7/8+$, then the algorithm obtained by reducing an $L$ instance, applying that algorithm, and recovering its solution always outputs an $L$-feasible solution and achieves value at least $1/2+$ whenever the $L$ optimum is at least $1-$.
hypotheses_covered: Encoded maximization problems L and S
Adapter satisfies instance mapping, feasibility recovery, optimum transfer, and value transfer conditions
Polynomial-time algorithm for S is a threshold approximation with output threshold 7/8+δ and optimum threshold 1−δ
caveat: The payload's rational symbols were corrupted in transmission; the statement uses δ for that parameter and spells out the corresponding adapter conditions.
